stick the landing: To complete a process in an impressive and conclusive manner.

To execute a flawless landing (of an aircraft, rocket, or space capsule).
stick to: To persist; to continue (to use, do, etc.)
To follow and remain close to.
stick to business: To concentrate on the important matters which are of present concern; to avoid becoming distracted or sidetracked.
stick to one's guns: To maintain one’s position or viewpoint when faced with opposition.
Of a gunner, to persist in faithfully attending to cannons while under fire.

stick to one's last: To stick to one's knitting (to concentrate on one's own tasks, affairs, area of expertise etc.).
stick to one's post: To remain in a position, especially in a critical situation.

stick to someone's ribs: To be filling, especially due to having a heavy meaty or glutinous consistency.
stick together: To remain united, to stay together in association or alliance.
To physically combine or join together by adhesion.
stick two fingers up: To give the V sign (a gesture of contempt or insult made by raising the index and middle fingers with the palm inwards).
stick up: To defy, to confront, to stand up to.
To be prominent; to point upwards.

stick up for: To speak or act in defence (of); to defend or protect.
stick up one's ass: A stiff, stern, uptight, or humorless manner.
stick weld: A weld created by the stick welding process.

stick welding: A method of manual electric welding that uses a consumable flux-covered electrode that forms a slag to protect the weld from oxygen degradation.
stick with: To persist in using or employing.
stick-in-the-mud: More generally, one who is slow, old-fashioned, or unprogressive; an old fogey.
sticker price: A price displayed on or near merchandise indicating a price at which the merchandise is offered for sale.
sticker shock: Disgust, shock, or fright upon learning the price of an item offered for sale.
stickiness: The property of sticking or adhering; adhesion.
Warmth and humidity, as on a muggy day.

The presence of unique attributes that make a product indisposable and valuable to its owner.
sticking plaster: An inadequate solution to a serious problem.
An adhesive bandage used in dressing wounds.

stickle: A sharp point; prickle; a spine
A shallow rapid in a river.
stickleback: Any one of numerous species of small fish of the family Gasterosteidae. The back is armed with two or more sharp spines. They inhabit both salt and brackish water, and construct nests from weeds.
stickler: A referee or adjudicator at a fight, wrestling match, duel, etc. who ensures fair play.
Someone who insistently advocates for something, especially for strict observance of a formal rule.
stickman: A simple drawing of a man with lines to represent limbs and torso.
A dealer in gambling who gathers the dice with a stick.
A player in a game played with a stick (such as hockey or lacrosse).
A person who makes confectionery by pulling candy onto a stick.
stickpin: An ornamented pin used to secure a necktie's end flat against the shirt, a tie tack.
sticks and stones: any obsolete technology (usually of military and law enforcement purposes) when used in comparison to state of the art technology used by the antagonists or competitors.

sticks in a bundle can't be broken: A group of people who are cooperating can succeed in a situation where an individual person cannot.
stickup: A small-diameter tree branch or limb that extends out of the water in flooded or submerged timber, as in a lake or river.
A wing collar with white bow tie, worn with school dress by distinguished senior boys at Eton College.
sticky bottle: A water bottle, handed from a car occupant to a cyclist during a race, illicitly used to aid the rider as he/she briefly maintains a grasp on the bottle while being carried along by the car.
sticky end: An unpleasant death, demise or conclusion, especially when deserved or brought about by one's own actions.
sticky note: A slip of paper, or a chit, with a gummy or gluey top that can be moved from place to place, usually as a reminder.

An (East) Asian man who is mostly attracted to other Asian men.
sticky toffee pudding: A British dessert consisting of moist sponge cake made with finely chopped dates, covered in a toffee sauce and often served with vanilla custard or ice-cream.
sticky wicket: A pitch that has become wet because of rain and therefore on which the ball bounces unpredictably.
stickybeak: An overly inquisitive person, a nosey parker.

stiff cheddar: A type of rennet cheese that is firm owing to the curds having been pressed or comminuted to a large degree to shed more whey and ripened for a longer time.
stiff neck: Discomfort or pain when trying to turn or move the neck.
stiff peaks: Firm tips (of whipping cream or egg whites) which have been beaten and are so aerated that they stand up straight.
stiff porridge: A porridge made with a greater proportion of meal or flour so as to achieve a thicker consistency, similar to dough (common in many African cuisines).
stiff shit: An unsympathetic retort to someone suffering misfortune.
stiff up: To apply rubber without oil as part of the French polishing process.

stiff upper lip: The quality of being resolute and showing self-restraint, stereotypically associated with the British; especially as keep a stiff upper lip.
stiff-necked: Having a stiff neck; suffering from torticollis
stiffen up: To become rigid, tense or stiff.

An alcoholic drink taken to fortify oneself.
stiffening: An item, material or feature that makes something stiffer.
stiffly: With stiffness; lacking a smooth flow of movement, or lacking movement altogether.
stifling: The act by which something is stifled.
stigmaria: Fossilized root structure of extinct tree-like plants.
stigmatise: To characterize as disgraceful or ignominious; to mark with a stigma or stigmata.
stilbene: Either of two isomeric hydrocarbons, diphenylethylene, but especially the trans isomer, used in the manufacture of dyes and many other compounds.
stile: A set of one or more steps surmounting a fence or wall, or a narrow gate or contrived passage through a fence or wall, which in either case allows people but not livestock to pass.
A vertical component of a frame or panel, such as that of a door, window, or ladder.
stiletto: A small, slender knife or dagger-like weapon intended for stabbing.
A woman's shoe with a tall, slender heel (called a stiletto heel).
